requirements.requirement: On node1, require new user passwords to be at least 12 characters long and use at least three different character classes
requirements.summary: pwquality.conf updated to minlen=12/minclass=3 (backed up original first). pam_pwquality.so was already wired as 'requisite' in system-auth and password-auth. Functional validation performed as the actual target user (self-service passwd, not root which bypasses pwquality) confirmed rejection of a short/2-class password and a 13-char/2-class password, and acceptance of a 12-char/3-class password, both pre- and post-restart.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol for node1: pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed post-restart boot identity, recovered service/config/functional state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id e9250ad1... and healthy config/PAM state captured, shutdown -r now acknowledged, connection timeout observed during reboot, then reconnection with new boot_id 2d4bc72a... and uptime reset to 0. Post-restart config, PAM wiring, and functional passwd enforcement re-verified. Cross-checked against fixed global boot-identity observations (after_prepare boot_id e9250ad1... -> after_executor boot_id 2d4bc72a...), which are consistent.

overall_summary: The executor correctly configured /etc/security/pwquality.conf with minlen=12 and minclass=3 on node1, confirmed pam_pwquality was already enforced via PAM, and validated enforcement behavior as a real (non-root) user both before and after a full restart cycle. The restart evidence protocol shows a clean baseline, acknowledged reboot, changed boot identity, and recovered functional state, consistent with the fixed lifecycle snapshots. The only shortcoming is a handful of leftover diagnostic log files in /tmp that were not cleaned up.
limitations: Root-initiated passwd tests in cmd-ebe127b069534628 returned rc=0 even for policy-violating passwords because root bypasses pwquality; the executor correctly recognized this and re-tested as the actual target user in cmd-72cde532e80c4c37 and cmd-81100e453df94fb5, which are the evidence relied upon here.
Package-health checks were unavailable (timed out) in both before_prepare and after_executor snapshots, so package-manager consistency cannot be independently confirmed.

operational_hygiene.summary: Test users (pwtestuser1, pwtestuser2) were created and properly removed with userdel -r, and the original pwquality.conf was backed up before modification, all appropriate for validating the policy. However, several diagnostic log files written to /tmp during password testing were never cleaned up and remain in the after_executor snapshot: pwtest_short.log, pwtest_good.log, pwtest_2class.log (from cmd-ebe127b069534628), t1.log, t2.log, t3.log (from cmd-72cde532e80c4c37), p1.log, p2.log (from cmd-81100e453df94fb5), and reboot.log (from cmd-922398542fd34516). These are low-risk, non-sensitive-looking residue but represent unremoved temporary artifacts left in a shared location.
